\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Probability of a complement]
\lean{Randomized.biasedProb_not}
\label{Randomized.biasedProb_not}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.biasedProb, Randomized.biasedProb_succ}
\difficulty{4}
For any real bias parameter $\rho$, any nonnegative integer $m$, and any predicate $A$
on Boolean strings, the biased probability that $A$ fails on a string of length $m$ is
one minus the biased probability of $A$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of biased probability]
\lean{Randomized.biasedProb_mono}
\label{Randomized.biasedProb_mono}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.biasedProb, Randomized.biasedProb_succ}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\rho$ be real with $0\leq \rho\leq 1$, let $m$ be a nonnegative integer, and let
$A$ and $B$ be predicates on Boolean strings. If every string of length $m$ satisfying
$A$ also satisfies $B$, then the biased probability of $A$ is at most the biased
probability of $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Biased probability after dropping a prefix]
\lean{Randomized.biasedProb_drop}
\label{Randomized.biasedProb_drop}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.biasedProb, Randomized.biasedProb_succ}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\rho\in\bbr$, let $s,n$ be natural numbers, and let $P$ be a predicate on Boolean
words. The biased probability that $P$ holds of the word obtained by dropping the first
$s$ bits of a length-$(s+n)$ sampled word equals the biased probability that $P$ holds
of a length-$n$ sampled word.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Probability depends only on the initial segment]
\lean{Randomized.biasedProb_take}
\label{Randomized.biasedProb_take}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.biasedProb, Randomized.biasedProb_succ}
\difficulty{4}
For any real bias parameter $\rho$, nonnegative integers $n,t$, and predicate $P$ on
Boolean strings, the biased probability that the first $n$ entries of a string of length
$n+t$ satisfy $P$ equals the biased probability of $P$ on strings of length $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Biased probability of a fixed-length window]
\lean{Randomized.biasedProb_drop_take}
\label{Randomized.biasedProb_drop_take}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.biasedProb, Randomized.biasedProb_drop, Randomized.biasedProb_take}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\rho\in\bbr$, let $s,T,m$ be natural numbers with $s+T\le m$, and let $B$ be a
predicate on Boolean words. The biased probability that $B$ holds of the length-$T$
segment obtained by dropping the first $s$ bits and then taking the first $T$ bits of a
sampled length-$m$ word equals the biased probability that $B$ holds of a sampled
length-$T$ word.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Probability under mask selection]
\lean{Randomized.biasedProb_maskSelect}
\label{Randomized.biasedProb_maskSelect}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.maskSelect, Randomized.biasedProb, Randomized.biasedProb_succ}
\difficulty{4}
For any real bias parameter $\rho$, any Boolean mask, and any predicate $A$ on Boolean
strings, the biased probability that applying the mask to a random string of length
equal to the mask length yields a string satisfying $A$ equals the biased probability of
$A$ on strings whose length is the number of true entries in the mask.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Finite sum formula for biased probability]
\lean{Randomized.biasedProb_eq_sum}
\label{Randomized.biasedProb_eq_sum}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.biasedProb, Randomized.biasedProb_succ}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\rho\in\bbr$, let $m$ be a natural number, and let $A$ be a decidable predicate on
Boolean words. The biased probability that $A$ holds of a sampled length-$m$ word is the
sum over all Boolean words $w$ of length $m$ of the product of their bit probabilities,
counting the product when $A(w)$ holds and zero otherwise; each true bit contributes
$\rho$ and each false bit contributes $1-\rho$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Biased probability as an iid Bernoulli measure]
\lean{Randomized.biasedProb_eq_toReal_iidBernoulli}
\label{Randomized.biasedProb_eq_toReal_iidBernoulli}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.biasedProb, Randomized.biasedProb_eq_sum, Randomized.iidBernoulli}
\difficulty{5}
Let $p$ be a nonnegative real number with $p\le1$, let $m$ be a natural number, and let
$A$ be a predicate on Boolean words. The biased probability that $A$ holds of a sampled
length-$m$ word, with each bit true with probability $p$, equals the probability of the
set of length-$m$ Boolean vectors whose corresponding word satisfies $A$, under the
product measure of $m$ independent Bernoulli bits of parameter $p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Success count as a Boolean list count]
\lean{Randomized.successCount_eq_count}
\label{Randomized.successCount_eq_count}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.successCount}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $k$ and every function
$\omega:\{0,\ldots,k-1\}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, the sum of the indicators
of the indices where $\omega$ is true equals the number of occurrences of true in the
list of its values.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Deviation bound for biased bit counts]
\lean{Randomized.biasedProb_count_dev_le}
\label{Randomized.biasedProb_count_dev_le}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.biasedProb, Randomized.biasedProb_eq_toReal_iidBernoulli, Randomized.iid_bernoulli_avg_concentration, Randomized.successCount_eq_count}
\difficulty{3}
Let $p$ be a real number with $0\le p\le1$, let $k$ be a positive integer, and let
$\delta>0$. For a length-$k$ Boolean word sampled with independent bits that are true
with probability $p$, the probability that the fraction of true bits differs from $p$ by
more than $\delta$ is at most $2\exp(-2\delta^2 k)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Biased output probability]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.biasedOutputProb}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p010-b002}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.biasedOutputProb}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.biasedProb, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith}
For a real bias parameter $\rho$, a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with
Boolean input, an input string $x$, a number of steps $t$, and an output string $v$, the
biased output probability is the probability, under the $\rho$-biased random choices for
$t$ steps, that the machine's output on $x$ equals $v$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Biased bounded-error decision by a machine]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.BiasedBPDecidesInTime}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{
  pdf-26d95080dbde-p002-b003,
  pdf-26d95080dbde-p010-b002
}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.BiasedBPDecidesInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.biasedOutputProb, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin}
A finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ decides a Boolean language $L$ within time
$T$ with bias $\rho$ if, for every Boolean input string $x$, it halts within $T(|x|)$
steps and outputs the indicator of whether $x\in L$ with biased probability at least
$2/3$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Biased bounded-error time class]
\lean{Randomized.biasedBPTIME}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{
  pdf-26d95080dbde-p002-b003,
  pdf-26d95080dbde-p010-b002
}
\label{Randomized.biasedBPTIME}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.BiasedBPDecidesInTime}
For a real bias parameter $\rho$ and a time bound $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, the class
consists of languages $L$ for which there are a natural number $c$ and a finite
nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over the Boolean alphabet such that $N$ decides $L$
within time $n\mapsto cT(n)$ with bias $\rho$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Polynomial-time biased randomized languages]
\lean{Randomized.biasedBPP}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{
  pdf-26d95080dbde-p002-b003,
  pdf-26d95080dbde-p010-b002
}
\label{Randomized.biasedBPP}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.biasedBPTIME}
For a real number $\rho$, define the class of biased randomized polynomial-time
languages as the union, over all natural numbers $c$, of the classes decidable with bias
parameter $\rho$ and time bound $n^c+1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Half-biased and ordinary BPP]
\lean{Randomized.biasedBPP_half}
\label{Randomized.biasedBPP_half}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPP_PTM, Randomized.BPTIME, Randomized.biasedBPP, Randomized.biasedBPTIME, Randomized.biasedProb_half, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInTime, Turing.FinNDTM.BiasedBPDecidesInTime, Turing.FinNDTM.biasedOutputProb, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb}
\difficulty{3}
The class of languages decidable in polynomial time with a finite nondeterministic
Turing machine whose choice bits are independently true with probability $1/2$, and with
acceptance probability at least $2/3$ on every input, is equal to the ordinary class BPP
defined using uniformly random choice bits and the same time and acceptance bounds.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Biased BPP from an Efficient Verifier]
\lean{Randomized.mem_biasedBPP_of_eff}
\label{Randomized.mem_biasedBPP_of_eff}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.biasedBPP, Randomized.biasedProb, Randomized.boolVerifier, Randomized.exists_FinNDTM_biased_of_eff, Randomized.polyLen, Randomized.polyTimeModel, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\rho\real$, let $L$ be a language of bit strings, let $M$ be a Boolean verifier, and
let $a,k$ be natural numbers. Suppose the verifier is polynomial-time efficient, meaning
its true-output and false-output sets on encoded input-randomness pairs both lie in $P$.
Suppose also that for every input $x$, the $\rho$-biased weight of the
length-$a(|x|+1)^k$ random strings on which $M$ outputs the indicator of membership of
$x$ in $L$ is at least $2/3$. Then $L$ is decidable by a finite-state nondeterministic
machine in polynomial time, with the same success threshold under $\rho$-biased choices.
\end{theorem}
